records.title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces
records.reason: S4 is a foundational general sequence-model architecture paper rather than an LLM inference/serving optimization paper; its main contribution is structured state-space sequence modeling and efficient training/evaluation across generic long-sequence tasks.
records.body_check: The paper develops S4 from continuous-time state-space models, derives an efficient structured parameterization and convolutional computation, and evaluates long-range sequence modeling. It does not target LLM serving, KV-cache management, decoding schedulers, model offload, or inference-system bottlenecks.

records.title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision
records.reason: Direct inference-kernel work: FlashAttention-3 redesigns attention for Hopper GPUs using asynchronous execution and low-precision paths, making it central to the kernel/runtime-compilation lineage.
records.body_check: The paper introduces Hopper-aware attention kernels that overlap tensor-core GEMM and softmax work and exploit FP8 while controlling numerical error. Evaluation is explicitly on attention throughput/accuracy and the kernel is used by later LLM serving systems for prefill/decode execution.

records.title: Ada-KV: Optimizing KV Cache Eviction by Adaptive Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Inference
records.reason: Direct KV-cache inference optimization: Ada-KV allocates cache budgets per attention head instead of uniformly and plugs into existing eviction methods.
records.body_check: The paper derives a loss upper bound for post-eviction attention, uses it to motivate head-wise adaptive KV budgets, and evaluates the method on RULER and LongBench in question-aware and question-agnostic settings. The final target is reduced KV memory during LLM inference while preserving quality.

records.title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into State-of-the-Art Pipelines
records.reason: DSPy is a programming and prompt-optimization framework for compound LM pipelines; it optimizes task quality/program parameters rather than the inference serving/runtime stack covered by this survey.
records.body_check: The paper defines declarative LM modules and compilers/teleprompters that optimize prompts and demonstrations against task metrics, with evaluations on LM pipelines. It does not introduce GPU scheduling, KV-cache, offload, inference kernels, quantization, or serving-resource mechanisms.

records.title: MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs
records.reason: Long-context LLM efficiency work: MoBA dynamically routes each query to selected context blocks, reducing attention computation while retaining the ability to switch between sparse and full attention.
records.body_check: The paper partitions context into blocks and applies learned query-to-block routing inspired by MoE, yielding sub-quadratic attention and reporting up to 16x speedup at very long context while maintaining full-attention-level performance; it also reports production long-context deployment.

records.title: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule
records.reason: The gated-delta mechanism yields linear-time sequence processing and has clear inference-efficiency implications, but the paper's primary contribution is a new sequence-model architecture and hardware-efficient training rather than an LLM inference-system mechanism.
records.body_check: The paper combines gating for memory erasure with a delta update rule for targeted state updates, supplies a parallel training algorithm, and evaluates language modeling, retrieval and long-context tasks against Mamba2/DeltaNet. Its efficiency contribution is architectural and training-oriented enough that inclusion in an inference-systems survey is not unequivocal.

records.title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
records.reason: Benchmark/evaluation work for long-term conversational memory rather than a KV-cache or inference-memory optimization method.
records.body_check: The paper constructs a benchmark for chat-assistant memory across multi-session interactions and evaluates systems/models on long-term information retention and use. It provides an evaluation target used by later memory/KV systems but does not itself propose an inference runtime, cache allocator, eviction algorithm, or serving optimization.

records.title: Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster AI Agents
records.reason: Direct agentic inference/runtime acceleration: it predicts likely future agent actions with faster models and executes API calls speculatively in parallel while preserving correctness.
records.body_check: The paper targets sequential tool/API latency in AI-agent execution, uses speculative action prediction plus verification to parallelize otherwise serial calls, and evaluates gaming, e-commerce, web-search and operating-system environments with reported speedups up to 30%. This fits agentic inference serving/runtime optimization.

records.title: Large Language Diffusion Models
records.reason: LLaDA is a foundational diffusion-language-model architecture/training paper whose main goal is demonstrating non-autoregressive language-model capability, not optimizing inference systems or serving efficiency.
records.body_check: The paper trains an 8B masked diffusion language model from scratch with forward masking and reverse masked-token prediction and evaluates general knowledge, math, code, in-context learning and instruction following. Although diffusion generation motivates later parallel-decoding systems, this paper itself does not contribute a serving scheduler, cache/offload mechanism, or inference kernel optimization.

records.title: Pushing Mixture of Experts to the Limit: Extremely Parameter Efficient MoE for Instruction Tuning
records.reason: Parameter-efficient instruction-tuning work: it uses MoE-style adapters to reduce trainable parameters, but its final objective is fine-tuning efficiency rather than MoE inference routing, expert placement, offload, or serving.
records.body_check: The paper studies extremely parameter-efficient MoE for instruction tuning and evaluates adaptation quality/parameter efficiency. The mechanism belongs to PEFT/training optimization; it does not address expert residency, inference communication, runtime routing latency, or inference memory hierarchy.
